concepts.label: Transaction-level failure classification (Java SDK) - TransactionFailedException / TransactionExpiredException / TransactionCommitAmbiguousException
concepts.reused_or_minted: reused - this is the dedicated page the promoted concept's own definition cites. It substantively matches, confirming the round's reuse hypothesis for this page, but also reveals the promoted label under-counts: the registry description names only TransactionFailedException/TransactionCommitAmbiguousException, while this page names THREE errors as a set ('There are three errors that transactions can raise to an application'), including TransactionExpiredException - see notable_absence.

concepts.label: Distributed ACID Transaction (Java SDK)
concepts.reused_or_minted: reused - the concept whose failure/commit outcomes this page classifies.

concepts.label: Background transaction cleanup
concepts.reused_or_minted: reused - minted in concept-docs/transactions-cleanup.json in this same batch; this page states the cleanup process is what eventually resolves a TransactionCommitAmbiguousException's ambiguity, one way or the other.

concepts.label: Staged mutation - transaction mutations held in a document's XATTRs until commit
concepts.reused_or_minted: reused - minted in concept-docs/transactions.json in this same batch; this page's timeout tradeoff is stated directly in terms of staged documents remaining locked.

concepts.label: TransactionResult.unstagingComplete() - a boolean flag indicating whether every document involved in a committed transaction has finished being unstaged (fully committed), as opposed to whether the transaction itself committed
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - a genuinely new, success-path signal, distinct from sdk:transaction-error-handling (which classifies FAILURE/ambiguity). A transaction can have definitely committed yet still report this flag false, which no existing concept captures.

concepts.label: Transaction timeout - the per-transaction-attempt Duration (default 15 seconds) after which retries stop and the attempt is abandoned, configurable via TransactionsConfig or transactionOptions()
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - a distinct configuration property from sdk:transaction-durability even though both are set through the same TransactionsConfig/transactionOptions() surface: this one is a Duration governing how long retries continue, not a DurabilityLevel governing write safety.

concepts.label: TransactionExpiredException - raised when retries continued until the transaction timeout was reached, as distinct from TransactionFailedException's fast-failure
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - named and distinguished as its own error on this page ('There are three errors that transactions can raise'), even though the promoted sdk:transaction-error-handling concept's registry label currently only lists the other two; captured as its own id so the distinction this page draws is not lost.

relations.subject: sdk:transaction-expired-exception
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - one of the three named members of the transaction-error-classification set this page documents
relations.evidence: `TransactionFailedException` indicates a fast-failure whereas `TransactionExpiredException` indicates that retries were made until the timeout was reached, but this distinction is not normally important to an application and generally `TransactionExpiredException` does not need to be handled individually.

relations.subject: sdk:transaction-timeout
relations.evidence: transaction timeouts (which default to 15 seconds) can be extended across the board through `TransactionsConfig`.

relations.subject: sdk:transaction-timeout
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - a longer timeout gives the protocol more time to resolve transient failures, at the cost of documents staying locked (staged) for longer
relations.evidence: The tradeoff to consider with longer timeouts, is that documents that have been staged by a transaction are effectively locked from modification from other transactions, until the timeout has been reached.

relations.subject: sdk:unstaging-complete-flag
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - a false flag is resolved by the same asynchronous background process, not by any explicit application action
relations.evidence: The cleanup process is asynchronously working to complete the commit, so that it will be fully visible to non-transactional actors.

relations.subject: sdk:transaction-error-handling
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - resolution of TransactionCommitAmbiguousException's ambiguity (whether the transaction actually committed) is delegated entirely to the background cleanup process
relations.evidence: If the transaction had in fact successfully reached the commit point, then the transaction will be fully completed ("unstaged") by the asynchronous cleanup process at some point in the future.

notable_absence.finding: The promoted sdk:transaction-error-handling concept's own registry label names only TransactionFailedException and TransactionCommitAmbiguousException. This page - its own dedicated source - explicitly states there are THREE errors transactions can raise ('There are three errors that transactions can raise to an application: * TransactionFailedException * TransactionExpiredException * TransactionCommitAmbiguousException'). TransactionExpiredException is a real, separately-named, separately-behaved member of the set (timeout-driven rather than fast-failure), not a paraphrase of TransactionFailedException. Flagging this as a candidate correction for the promoted concept's definition at reconciliation, rather than silently absorbing TransactionExpiredException into the existing two-exception description.

cross_component_finding: This page substantively reuses sdk:transaction-error-handling exactly as promoted, confirming the round's hypothesis for this page - but it also depends on sdk:transaction-cleanup (minted for concept-docs/transactions-cleanup.json, a page describing a mechanism none of the four promoted transaction concepts touch) to explain what actually happens after a TransactionCommitAmbiguousException or a false unstagingComplete() flag: resolution in BOTH cases is handed off entirely to the asynchronous cleanup process, never to an application-visible retry or explicit action. This threads all three of this batch's transaction pages together: transactions.json introduces staged mutations and points to cleanup; transactions-cleanup.json defines what cleanup actually does; this page shows cleanup being the thing that quietly resolves the ambiguity transaction error handling can't resolve synchronously.
cross_product_finding: This page has no links or references to the SQL++/Query-service transaction error-handling story (n1ql:transactions, n1ql:commit-transaction, n1ql:rollback-transaction) at all, even though those statements can raise their own analogous failure states on the cbq shell. The SDK's and SQL++'s transaction error-handling documentation remain two fully separate silos in this corpus, with no cross-reference drawn in either direction from this page.
